Well-Defined Problems
Well-defined problems can be created from opportunities

A needs statement can be used to formulate a well-defined problem, thus making the criteria for a successful solution clear as well
Even if the circumstances are complex or complicated
Even if the solution is hard to devise and requires magical thinking
The solution can be incremental or radical
And can sometimes lead to a dramatically new product class or market

Critical: any solution to a well-defined problem must be falsifiable

You Have a Well-Defined Problem When…
You have a clear statement (story) of the 5 W’s, especially:
What is the use case(s)
Who is the user(s) (and any other key stakeholders)
Why does the user(s) has/have the problem
You know what the solution needs to deliver:
Pains relieved
Gains achieved
Think in terms of specific and measurable outcomes
And you also know (if possible):
The time to deliver the solution
The cost to deliver the solution
Likely impediments to creating or delivering any solution
Example: How can we help… do… under these circumstances… in order to accomplish…?
